dossier_sections.heading: Company description
dossier_sections.text: COMPANY DESCRIPTION:What started as a failing joint venture between ASM International and Philips in a leaky shed, widely dismissed even by the engineers who worked there, ASML eventually became the sole supplier of one of the most critical tools in the entire global semiconductor supply chain.ASML is a capital equipment company with a dominant position in deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines and sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. Lithography machines are tools used by chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung and Intel to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips. While the business mix is diversified by region, system and technology, the customer base is highly concentrated, with TSMC and Samsung representing 38% of total sales in 2025 (24% and 14%, respectively). Geographically, sales are split between China (41%), Taiwan (36%), Korea (35%) and the US (18%) with the balance in Japan, EMEA and the rest of Asia. By system, half of sales are generated from DUV machines and half are generated from EUV machines. 25% of total sales are install base management, which is essentially their aftermarket and servicing business. This includes maintenance and field service (ASML technicians are often embedded at customer fabs for regular upkeep), software upgrades, hardware (physical) upgrades and parts and consumables (for components that need to be replaced over time). Services grow as the install base grows, are recurring in nature, are less cyclical and provide a floor during downturns.

dossier_sections.heading: Why we own it
dossier_sections.text: Why we own ASML is the sole supplier of one of the most critical tools in the entire global semiconductor supply chain. Specifically, ASML is a capital equipment company with a dominant position in deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines and sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. Lithography machines are tools used by chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung and Intel to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips. While volumes are relatively low (500+ unit sales annually), the price for a leading edge EUV machine is north of $200mn. Chips are the building blocks for the digital economy, powering everything from smartphones and computers to datacenters, cars and medical devices, which is a substantial tailwind to the business. Semiconductor industry sales are expected to reach $1.5tn this year and could top $2tn by the end of the decade. ASML’s technology is the embodiment of accumulated engineering knowledge across hundreds of interdependent subsystems (laser physics, vacuum engineering, mirror optics, etc.) which took decades of effort and significant resources to master. With a dominant position in its part of the value chain (90% of the DUV lithography market and 100% of EUV), derived from high switching costs and deeply entrenched customer relationships, ASML benefits from the ever-increasing pervasiveness of chips. While the semiconductor industry is inherently cyclical, much like TSMC, the most advanced modern technology does not exist without ASML, and it should remain a core position.

dossier_sections.heading: Positives
dossier_sections.text: Positives - Total net sales of €9.3B were above the €8.4-9.0B guided range, up 21% year-over-year (€7.7B in Q2 2025) and 6% sequentially (€8.8B in Q1 2026). Gross margin of 54% exceeded the 51-53% guided range. Net income rose 26% year-over-year to €2.9B (basic EPS of €7.59). Installed Base Management (service) sales of €2.76B came in roughly €300M above guidance, underscoring a high-margin, recurring revenue engine that management expects to grow >30% annually. Full-year 2026 outlook lifted to €43- 45B net sales and 54-56% gross margin, the second upward revision in 2026. Intel Foundry reached a production milestone using High-NA EUV on its 18A process for Core Ultra Series 3 chips, which is the first concrete commercial validation of the platform. Management said ASML has “already received substantially all orders needed for 2027 and a large number of orders for 2028,” a multi-year demand signal well beyond the normal order book. On capital returns, the interim dividend was raised to €1.88/share (from €1.60 in the prior interim), plus €1.1B of share buybacks in the quarter.

dossier_sections.heading: Negatives
dossier_sections.text: Negatives - Shares fell 3.8% following the print despite the beat-and-raise, reflecting the demanding scale of the implied second-half ramp and unresolved China policy risk. First-half 2026 free cash flow was negative (€1.3B) despite €5.7B of net income over the same period, as inventory and prepayments built ahead of the H2 shipment ramp. The raised full-year guidance implies €14B+ of net sales in Q4 2026 alone, an unusually demanding execution requirement in a single quarter. EUV fell to 57% of system sales in Q2 (from 66% in Q1) as DUV/immersion (29%) and metrology gained share. Not necessarily negative, but a reminder that near-term mix will swing quarter to quarter. A small number of customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and memory makers) continue to account for the large majority of sales (roughly 61% from the top four customers in 2025).

dossier_sections.heading: Special items
dossier_sections.text: Special items: ASMLhas granted a “stichting”, or preference share option, to a Dutch foundation established under Netherlands law that acts as a poison pill defense mechanism. This protects ASML’s independence and long-term strategic orientation (which is important for a company that sits at the center of global geopolitical contest over semiconductor technology). It also means ordinary shareholders have limited ability to influence change. The Dutch government has also made clear through policy signals that ASML is a strategic national asset, adding another layer of implicit protection beyond the preference share option.
